title: Therapeutic application of virtual reality in a pulmonary clinic
summary:
This observational study at the Thoraxklinik Heidelberg is investigating how effectively virtual reality (VR) with relaxing content can be used in the care of patients at a specialist lung clinic. The study is being conducted in various areas of the specialist lung clinic, including the intensive care unit, weaning ward, surgical ward, pneumology ward and palliative care ward. The aim is to assess the acceptance of VR technology among patients and hospital staff and its impact on patients' well-being and symptoms. Approximately 10 participants per ward will be recruited and staff trained in the VR application will support the use of the VR glasses.
The study records objective data such as heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation and medication requirements as well as subjective impressions. The latter are recorded using various questionnaires, including the numerical rating scale (NRS) on pain intensity, the multidimensional Brief Pain Inventory (BPI) on pain quality, the current mood scale (ASTS) to record the current state of mind and the distress thermometer to assess perceived stress. To take part in the study, patients must be of legal age and willing to use VR technology.
conditions: The study investigates the influence of VR applications in the treatment of various lung diseases.

interventions.name:
VR application on patients on various wards at the Thoraxklinik Heidelberg. After each application on the respective wards, the participants and the hospital staff who carried out the VR application were asked about their experiences with the VR application using a questionnaire.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria for patients
-Age ≥ 18 years
-Sufficient cognitive ability to understand the meaning and purpose of the study
- Sufficient decision-making capacity
- Ability to give informed consent

Inclusion criteria for clinical staff
-Age ≥ 18 years
-Employed by the Thoraxklinik Heidelberg
-Trained in the use of the VR glasses
-Informed about the study
Exclusion criteria:
Patient exclusion criteria
- Treating or caring hospital staff consider
the patient is not suitable for the study
- not in full possession of his/her mental faculties
- Not able to consent to the study
- Migraine
- Taking opioids (only in the intensive care unit)
- Epilepsy
- Severe mental illness
- Dementia, Parkinson's disease
- Delirium
- Known motion sickness
- Post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV)
